# WorthPlaying — contemporary review

- Original source: [WorthPlaying — contemporary review](https://www.worthplaying.com/article/2002/12/16/reviews/7395-pc-review-robin-hood/)
- Author / publication: Tony “OUberLord” Mitera / WorthPlaying
- Language / date: English; 2002-12-16
- Access: Full review page retrieved directly
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: none found in the Wayback Machine (checked 2026-09-09)
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (commercial review, not transcribed)

**Score: 8.6/10.**

Mitera considers the game a successful use of the Robin Hood legend within the squad-tactics format. He highlights its lighter mood compared with Commandos while stressing that a humorous presentation does not make the missions effortless.

The review favors intuitive controls that let the player concentrate on party management and tactics. Its conclusion recommends the game to patient players interested in tactical games or the legend, while acknowledging that even adjustable difficulty will not suit everyone.

**Research use:** contemporary evidence for how the game's accessibility, tone, and difficulty were perceived. The judgment belongs to the reviewer and is not a measurement of the underlying systems.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: "PC Review - 'Robin Hood'" by Tony "OUberLord" Mitera, 16 December 2002, 9:03 a.m. PST; box data given as genre Real Time Strategy, publisher Strategy First and Wanadoo, developer Spellbound Studios, release 15 November 2002; score 8.6/10; about 25 screenshots. Commercial review, so paraphrased.

- Opening: the legend teaches justice, honour, charity, forgiveness; earlier Robin Hood games were not bad, but this one outshines most.
- Genre: top-down tactics like Commandos, but lighter in tone while not easy. Long recap of the legend (Richard's crusade, Prince John regent, capture by Duke Leopold, ransom, father dead, lands taken by the sheriff, heavy taxes).
- Controls: left-click selects, right-click acts; on-screen icons and hotkeys. Robin fights with sword, shoots the bow, throws purses to distract "the dumber guards", and knocks out from behind. Generic types: Strong Merry whistles, carries bodies or objects, eats to heal, triggers traps from a distance; Aggressive Merry throws apples, picks locks, revives comrades, finishes enemies; Mustachioed Merry uses bow, shield, and hog-ties unconscious guards. Others: pay beggars for information, climb vines, give a leg up, search bodies. Everyone can run, walk or crawl, which affects both visibility and noise.
- Persistence: items, health and money carry across missions; kills are tracked and reduce recruitment; stealthy players get more Merry Men than they can use.
- Sherwood: camp for rest, talking to comrades, and checking the map for the sheriff's convoys; team selected per mission; some missions solo, some need particular abilities. Convoy ambush described: the team waits under leaves, AI groups of three in the trees, a log on a rope swings down onto the wagon, guards fan out; arrows at targets near the hidden groups release them. Story missions harder because the next objective is rarely clear; trial and error.
- Camp tasks: arrows, apples, nets, melee and archery training, resting.
- Melee: characters only block until told to attack; hold left button and draw shapes: a line toward the enemy is a slow strong jab, dragging away a quicker stab, semicircles and full circles sweep 180 and (as printed) 260 degrees, an infinity sign is the most powerful attack; each attack drains stamina, and a character with none left stands dazed and open. Combat usually kills rather than knocks out, so avoid it if you want recruits.
- Graphics on par with the genre, nothing flashy, everything recognisable; menus and dialogue boxes use wax seals instead of buttons. Sound average but not cheap; memorable score. Controls simple yet complete.
- Verdict: not for the impatient or for those wanting an easy game; difficulty configurable; called possibly the best Robin Hood game yet; "a good buy" for a lighthearted tactical game.
